title: The Tap That Counts, Explained
subtitle: Casimir Beng, Solveig Adeyemi and Mirela Hanke on what strata residents do when the intercom's compliance alert fires
summary: A research explainer from the School of Continuous Improvement on Casimir Beng, Solveig Adeyemi and Mirela Hanke's interview study of what strata residents do when a shared intercom's security-compliance notification fires. It follows a single alert from the visitor's buzz to the resident's tap, then sets the audit's near-total acknowledgement rate beside what sixty-four residents say they actually do with it. All three authors describe the work in their own words.
topic: A research explainer of the paper interviewing strata residents about what they do when the shared intercom's security-compliance notification fires, set against the audit's own near-total acknowledgement rate and its falling time-to-acknowledge

beats.text: A five-minute window was built to ask whether someone checked the door. It was never built to notice that the fastest possible tap and the least attentive one have become the same gesture.
